The proposed answer has a sign error, so it is incorrect.

The solution uses Δₓ ∫ log|x−y| u(y) dy = −2π u(x). The fundamental solution of the Laplacian in ℝ² is (1/2π) log|x|, so Δ log|x| = 2π δ. The correct identity is therefore Δₓ ∫ log|x−y| u(y) dy = +2π u(x).

Redoing the computation with the kernel f(x) + f(y) − log|x−y|, where f = log w:

- The eigenvalue-0 equation is I₁ f(x) + I₂ − ∫ log|x−y| u(y) dy = 0.
- Applying Δ gives I₁ C − 2π u(x) = 0, so u(x) = C I₁ / (2π), which is constant.
- Writing u ≡ k ≠ 0, we get I₁ = k|Ω|, so k = C k |Ω| / (2π).
- Hence C = 2π/|Ω|.

The correct value is C = 2π/|Ω|, not −2π/|Ω|.

VERDICT: REJECT
